newsitem.title: GREECE: ALBANIAN PRESIDENT SEES CALM RETURNING AFTER RIOTS.
newsitem.headline: ALBANIAN PRESIDENT SEES CALM RETURNING AFTER RIOTS.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha said calm will return to his troubled Balkan country after rioting investors in collapsed pyramid schemes start getting some of their money back.
"Things will calm down after people get money from the assets of two such 'companies' that we have frozen," he told the Athens daily Ta Nea in an interview published on Monday.
"Of course it is understandable that such a huge amount in cash cannot be handed out in a few days. The neediest will be compensated first," he was quoted as saying.
Berisha faces nearly daily street riots and concerted attacks by political opposition parties over the collapsed schemes that have left many Albanians destitute.

The protesters accuse Berisha and his government of failing to warn investors of the pitfalls of such schemes which have attracted the savings of virtually every family in Albania since it emerged from 50 years of Stalinist isolation six years ago.

"Albania must be rid of these pyramid schemes, which developed excessively, primarily because of lack of legislation," he said. "I was personally concerned that no state institution was involved and indeed it was not."
Berisha said the violent riots gripping Europe's poorest state were due to people's despair and the feeling that they had been abused.

"That first week people's situation was desperate and the distribution of money had not yet started," he said. "I think that those who abused the people made a big political mistake. We must understand that this is how capitalism works."
